slides.headline: Still know who you met by Friday.
slides.sub: You met twelve people. By Friday you can name two. Forty seconds after each conversation fixes it. Six things, in order. A pen works.

slides.headline: Write their name and one thing they said.
slides.lede: Not the job title. The title is on the badge. The line is what you will recognise them by, and what you open with when you write.

items.label: Like this
items.prompt: Sarah, Bristol, hates the word synergy.

slides.headline: Write what they asked you for.
slides.lede: In their words. If they asked for nothing, write that too. It tells you what kind of conversation it was.

items.label: Like this
items.prompt: The name of the supplier. The article. Word for word.

slides.headline: Write what you promised.
slides.lede: The exact thing, with the day. Most follow-ups die here: you remember a warm conversation and forget the offer you made inside it.

slides.headline: Write the one line you would introduce them with.
slides.lede: If you cannot write it, you did not find out who they are. Go back and ask one more question.

items.label: Like this
items.prompt: Sarah runs ops for a Bristol logistics firm and knows the market.

slides.headline: Put the follow-up in the calendar now.
slides.lede: Before the next conversation, not at the end of the night. Nine tomorrow, with their line in the reminder, so you know what to say.

slides.headline: Send it tonight. Two lines, their words.
slides.lede: The thing they said and the thing you promised. Nothing about you. Almost nobody does this, so you are remembered.

items.label: Like this
items.prompt: Good to meet you, Sarah. Deck attached, as promised, and no synergy in it.

slides.headline: A pen works. Convu does it from a voice note.
slides.body: Thirty seconds on the walk to the station.

slides.headline: One of these a week. Something you can use before Friday.
